subject: [RFC PATCH 36/57] mm/collapse: report what the scan found

2026-08-16.patch_summary: This patch adds a new trace event called mm_collapse_scan to report the results of an anonymous memory scan in the Linux kernel. The scan reports information such as the address scanned, the number of holes or zero-page slots, the number of swapped-out pages, and the orders that survived the scan. This information is used to determine whether a table should be refused outright or if it can still try certain orders. The patch also adds a new function called trace_mm_collapse_scan to report this information through tracing. This patch is part of a larger series of patches (36/57) and aims to improve the reporting and debugging capabilities of the kernel's memory management system.
